emily (support): FYI customer reported batch /rerank returning shifted scores and wrong candidate counts per query. they attached request id and payload.

emily (support): Request ID: abc123-redwood. They say each query had 3 candidates but response shows 2 then 4. 200 OK from API, but alignment off. payload:
```json
{
  "batch": [
    {"query_id": "q-1", "candidates": ["docA", "docB", "docC"]},
    {"query_id": "q-2", "candidates": ["docD", "docE", "docF"]},
    {"query_id": "q-3", "candidates": ["docG", "docH", "docI"]}
  ]
}
```

ops-bot: New ticket #SUP-1289 created for Request ID abc123-redwood :ticket: 

sam (eng): @emily can you paste the raw response body (scores + meta) and the exact curl you used? curious if this is a client-side flattening or server serialization issue.

emily (support): raw response (redacted):
```json
{
  "results": [
    {"query_id": "q-1", "scores": [0.92, 0.88, 0.77]},
    {"query_id": "q-2", "scores": [0.95, 0.80]},
    {"query_id": "q-3", "scores": [0.66, 0.60, 0.58, 0.51]}
  ]
}
```

emily (support): note: API returned 200 and no top-level error. customer observed app matched scores to wrong docs (q-2 got last 2 scores from q-1+2 mix).

mira (repro): I pushed a tiny repro script and can trigger locally. quick curl I used to reproduce: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"batch":[{"query_id":"q-1","candidates":["a","b","c"]},{"query_id":"q-2","candidates":["d","e","f"]}]}'
```

mira (repro): In my debug logs I see server-side flatten step: `flatten_candidates(batch) -> flat_list` then a reorder loop that uses an off-by-one index when reconstructing per-query slices. likely bug in multiplex path when chunking >1 queries into same worker.

sam (eng): thanks @mira. can you paste the stack snippet where the offset is computed? also any hint if this correlates with enabling `multiplex=true` flag?

mira (repro): stack excerpt: `for i in range(len(batch)): end = offsets[i+1]  # oops` — offsets array length = len(batch) so offsets[i+1] is out of bounds for last item, but Python wrapped it into next chunk when running in C extension; leads to shifted slice.

luis (sre): did this cause retries or spikes? any latency anomalies?

emily (support): customer saw 4x calls due to retries in their client and a billing spike overnight. they manually rolled back to single-query endpoint to stop costs.

luis (sre): ok we should throttle multiplexing for affected tenants and rollback server-side to the previous variant. i'll schedule a hotfix deployment.

sam (eng): quick mitigation we can do today: validate that sum(len(candidates)) == sum(expected_counts) before forwarding to worker; return 400 with `per_query_candidate_mismatch` if not. opened PR #3421 with validation + unit test.

ops-bot: PR #3421 opened by sam (eng) — ready for review.

emily (support): i'll share this with the customer and ask them to retry once patch is live, and will offer billing credit for the retry-induced overage.

luis (sre): rolling patch to canary in us-west and reservation of dedicated pool disabled for multiplex for now. will update when canary green.

emily (support): thanks everyone — keeping the customer posted. I'll create a postmortem after fix. :white_check_mark:
